topic: PM Modi Became India's Longest Continuously Serving Elected PM

subtopics.title: Modi's Record-Breaking Continuous Tenure
subtopics.summary: Narendra Modi became India's longest continuously serving elected Prime Minister after completing 4,399 consecutive days in office since 26 May 2014. He surpassed the uninterrupted tenure record held by Jawaharlal Nehru. The milestone is the longest uninterrupted period served by a democratically elected Prime Minister in independent India.
facts: Modi completed 4,399 consecutive days in office.
He has been in office since 26 May 2014.
He surpassed the uninterrupted tenure record held by Jawaharlal Nehru.
It is the longest uninterrupted period served by a democratically elected PM in independent India.
Nehru's overall tenure as Prime Minister lasted approximately 6,131 days.
Nehru's cumulative tenure includes his time as PM of the Interim Government.
Gulzari Lal Nanda was interim PM on both occasions.

subtopics.title: Constitutional Position of the Prime Minister
subtopics.summary: The Prime Minister is the head of the Union Government and the leader of the Council of Ministers. The booklet describes the PM as head of the executive, chairperson of the Union Cabinet and chief coordinator of government policy and administration. Article 74 provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the PM to aid and advise the President, while Article 75 deals with the appointment, tenure and responsibilities of the PM and the Council of Ministers.
facts: The PM is the Head of the Executive.
The PM is the Chairperson of the Union Cabinet.
The PM is Head of the Union Government and leader of the Council of Ministers.
The PM is the chief coordinator of government policy and administration.
If a member of Lok Sabha, the PM is its leader.
Article 74 provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the PM to aid and advise the President.
Article 75 deals with the appointment, tenure and responsibilities of the PM and Council of Ministers.
Article 163 establishes State Councils of Ministers led by the Chief Minister to aid and advise the Governor.

subtopics.title: Appointment, Tenure and the Council of Ministers
subtopics.summary: The President appoints the PM but is not free in the selection, and normally invites the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha to form the government. If no single party has a clear majority, the President invites a person likely to command support of two or more parties that make up a Lok Sabha majority. The PM holds office during the pleasure of the President but cannot be dismissed while enjoying majority support in the Lok Sabha. Rules for the Council of Ministers include a 15% size cap and a six-month limit for ministers who are not in Parliament.
facts: The President normally invites the leader of the majority party to form the government.
If no single party has a clear majority, the President invites a person who can command support of two or more parties forming a Lok Sabha majority.

The size of the Council of Ministers cannot exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha (91st Amendment, 2003).
A minister who is not in Parliament for six months will lose their position.
Article 88 allows ministers to take part in both Houses but does not guarantee them voting rights.

subtopics.title: Modi's Firsts and Records in Context
subtopics.summary: Modi is the first Indian PM born after 15 August 1947 and the longest-serving PM from outside the Indian National Congress. He is among the few Indian PMs to secure three consecutive electoral mandates at the Union level. In 2014, the BJP-led NDA won an absolute majority of 336 out of 543 Lok Sabha seats, which the booklet calls the first Non-Congress single party majority government.
facts: Modi is the first Indian PM born after 15 August 1947.
Modi is the longest-serving PM from outside the Indian National Congress.
Modi is among the few Indian PMs to secure 3 consecutive electoral mandates at the Union level.
Modi is the 3rd PM after Nehru and Indira Gandhi to serve 3 terms.
In 2014, the BJP-led NDA got an absolute majority of 336 out of 543 Lok Sabha seats.
The 2014 government is described as the first Non-Congress single party majority government.
The BJP became the first party since 1984 to get a majority in the Lok Sabha.
Morarji Desai was India's first Non-Congress PM and its oldest PM at 81 years.
Rajiv Gandhi was India's youngest PM at 40 years.
V.P. Singh was the first PM to leave office following a no-confidence vote.

quizzes.passage: Appointing a Prime Minister is one of the first steps in forming a government in India. The Constitution says the President makes the appointment, but the President does not have complete freedom in the selection. In ordinary circumstances, the President invites the leader of the party that holds a majority in the Lok Sabha. If no single party has a clear majority, the President has to decide whom to invite by judging who is likely to win the confidence of the House. The Prime Minister holds office during the pleasure of the President. The Prime Minister leads a team of ministers known as the Council of Ministers. This team includes Cabinet Ministers, who are senior members placed below the Prime Minister, along with Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers. Each group has its own role in running government departments. Ministers may sit in Parliament or be appointed from outside it for a limited period. Ministers of State are one of the categories within this team, and the booklet describes their roles in detail. Taken together, these arrangements explain how the executive is formed, how the Prime Minister's position is structured, and how ministers take part in the work of Parliament.

quizzes.passage: The Constitution provides for the appointment of the Prime Minister by the President, but the President's choice is shaped by the political situation in the Lok Sabha. Normally, the leader of the majority party is invited to form the government. When no party has a clear majority, the President looks for a person who can attract support from a combination of parties. The Prime Minister heads the government and guides its policy. Ministers are then chosen to help run the government, and the booklet lists several categories among them. Some ministers hold independent charge of ministries, while others assist senior ministers in their work. A minister who is not a member of Parliament has a limited time to become one. The booklet also notes that ministers may take part in the proceedings of both Houses without a guaranteed right to vote. The size of the council is restricted by a constitutional amendment, and the salary of the Prime Minister is set by law. Constitutional provisions on these matters are set out in several Articles, which the booklet links to each rule. The booklet also describes the Prime Minister as the head of the executive and the leader of the Council of Ministers. Together, these points give a basic picture of how the executive functions at the Union level.

quizzes.passage: Narendra Modi became India's longest continuously serving elected Prime Minister after completing 4,399 consecutive days in office. He had taken office on 26 May 2014, and this period surpassed the uninterrupted record held by Jawaharlal Nehru. The booklet explains that Nehru's overall tenure as Prime Minister lasted about 6,131 days, but that this total includes time when he served as head of an interim government before the first general elections. The Lok Sabha has 543 seats, and the party or alliance that commands a majority is normally called upon to form the government. Several Prime Ministers of India are noted for records that the booklet describes in short facts. These facts include the age at which a Prime Minister took office, the years in which the Prime Minister served, and the house of Parliament from which a Prime Minister came. Modi's record is described in the context of the country's general elections, and the booklet measures it in days rather than years. The booklet also notes that Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India and the first to die in office. Taken together, these facts give a useful picture of how the record of India's Prime Ministers can be compared.

quizzes.passage: Narendra Modi has been Prime Minister since 26 May 2014, and his uninterrupted service has drawn attention in the booklet. The booklet also places him in a wider context of Prime Ministers who came from different backgrounds. Some of them took office at a young age, while others were very old when they became Prime Minister. A few Prime Ministers left office in unusual ways, and some held the post for only a very short time. The Lok Sabha has 543 seats, and the booklet records how many of those seats the 2014 alliance won. Several Prime Ministers also came from South India, and their origins are noted in the booklet. The booklet presents these details in short factual notes, which makes it possible to compare the careers of different leaders. The booklet also records that Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister and that Lal Bahadur Shastri was the second to die in office. Its notes on Nehru also mention that his overall tenure is recorded as about 6,131 days, including his period as interim Prime Minister before the first general elections. Taken together, the examples show the range of experience among India's Prime Ministers and the variety of paths they followed to office.
